context.title: Hezekiah Reopens the Temple
context.summary: In his first month as king, Hezekiah reopens the temple doors his father shut. The Levites cleanse it, sin offerings are made for all Israel, and worship with David's music resumes.
context.background: The cleansing took sixteen days (v. 17). Because too few priests were ready, Levites helped — Chronicles notes they were 'more upright in heart' about sanctifying themselves (v. 34). Songs used 'the words of David, and of Asaph the seer' (v. 30).

customs.note: Worshipers placed hands on a sin offering, identifying themselves with it (compare Leviticus 4:24).

watchFor: Hezekiah acts in 'the first year... in the first month' (v. 3).
The offering is for 'all Israel,' north and south (v. 24).

w: and they made a sin offering

people.name: Hezekiah
people.summary: Son of Ahaz (2 Kings 18:1; 2 Chr. 29:1), whom he succeeded on the throne of the kingdom of Judah. He reigned twenty-nine years (B.C. 726-697).

people.name: Abijah
people.summary: The daughter of Zechariah (2 Chr. 29:1; comp. Isa. 8:2), and afterwards the wife of Ahaz.

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: The father of Abijah, who was the mother of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:1).

people.name: David
people.summary: Beloved, the eighth and youngest son of Jesse, a citizen of Bethlehem. His father seems to have been a man in humble life. His mother’s name is not recorded.

people.name: Merari
people.summary: Sad; bitter, the youngest son of Levi, born before the descent of Jacob into Egypt, and one of the seventy who accompanied him thither (Gen. 46:11; Ex. 6:16).

people.name: Amasai
people.summary: The father of a Levite, one of the two Kohathites who took a prominent part at the instance of Hezekiah in the cleansing of the temple (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Azariah
people.summary: Son of Jehallelel.

people.name: Eden
people.summary: Son of Joah, and one of the Levites who assisted in reforming the public worship of the sanctuary in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Jehalelel
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Joah
people.summary: A descendant of Gershom.

people.name: Joah
people.summary: Son of Zimmah.

people.name: Joel
people.summary: Son of Azariah.

people.name: Kish
people.summary: A Levite in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Mahath
people.summary: Another Kohathite Levite, of the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Zimmah
people.summary: The father of Joah (2 Chr. 29:12).

people.name: Asaph
people.summary: A Levite; one of the leaders of David’s choir (1 Chr. 6:39). Psalms 50 and 73-83 inclusive are attributed to him. He is mentioned along with David as skilled in music, and a “seer” (2 Chr. 29:30).

people.name: Mattaniah
people.summary: A Levite who assisted in purifying the temple at the reformation under Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

people.name: Shimri
people.summary: Assisted at the purification of the temple in the time of Hezekiah (2 Chr. 29:13).

people.name: Zechariah
people.summary: Hebrew prophet.

people.name: Jeduthun
people.summary: A Levite of the family of Merari, one of the leaders of the temple music (1 Chr. 6:44; 15:17, 19). He was probably the same as Jeduthun.

people.name: Heman
people.summary: Grandson of Samuel (1 Chr. 6:33; 15:17), to whom the 88th Psalm probably was inscribed.

people.name: Jehiel
people.summary: One of the Levites of the family of Heman who assisted Hezekiah in his work of reformation (2 Chr. 29:14).

people.name: Shemaiah
people.summary: A Levite (2 Chr. 29:14).

people.name: Shimei
people.summary: One of the sons of Heman, who assisted in the purification of the temple (2 Chr. 29:14).

people.name: Uzziel
people.summary: A son of Jeduthan (2 Chr. 29:14).

people.name: Ahaz
people.summary: The son and successor of Jotham, king of Judah (2 Kings 16; Isa. 7-9; 2 Chr. 28). He gave himself up to a life of wickedness and idolatry. Notwithstanding the remonstrances and warnings of Isaiah, Hosea, and Micah, he appealed for help against Rezin, king of Damascus, and Pekah, king of Israel, who threatened Jerusalem, to Tiglath-pileser, the king of Assyria, to the great injury of his kingdom and his own humilating subjection to the Assyrians (2 Kings 16:7, 9; 15:29).

people.name: Aaron
people.summary: The eldest son of Amram and Jochebed, a daughter of Levi (Ex. 6:20). Some explain the name as meaning mountaineer, others mountain of strength, illuminator.

people.name: Nathan
people.summary: A prophet in the reigns of David and Solomon (2 Chr. 9:29). He is first spoken of in connection with the arrangements David made for the building of the temple (2 Sam. 7:2, 3, 17), and next appears as the reprover of David on account of his sin with Bathsheba (12:1-14).

people.name: Gad
people.summary: A prophet who joined David in the “hold,” and at whose advice he quitted it for the forest of Hareth (1 Chr. 29:29; 2 Chr. 29:25; 1 Sam. 22:5).

places.name: Jerusalem
places.summary: Called also Salem, Ariel, Jebus, the “city of God,” the “holy city;” by the modern Arabs el-Khuds, meaning “the holy;” once “the city of Judah” (2 Chr. 25:28).

places.name: Holy Place
places.summary: One of the two portions into which the tabernacle was divided (Ex. 26:31; 37:17-25; Heb. 9:2). It was 20 cubits long and 10 in height and breadth.

places.name: Kidron
places.summary: Kedron = Cedron, turbid, the winter torrent which flows through the Valley of Jehoshaphat, on the eastern side of Jerusalem, between the city and the Mount of Olives.
